summary:
This application is the backend for a small online shop that sells products out of one shared database. Shoppers browse a catalog of products, organized into categories, see current prices, and place orders that record priced line items; each order can then be paid for, creating a payment charge linked back to that specific order. Behind the scenes, placing an order looks up catalog pricing, reserves the needed stock, and checks that the customer's account is in good standing before the order and its line items are recorded.

The primary users are shoppers/customers who browse the catalog, place orders, and pay for them. Staff can look up a customer's account record via a dedicated lookup, though the evidence only shows a read capability here, not an account-management action (no method to change a customer's active status was found, only a read-only IsActive check used internally).

Structurally the system is a thin backend organized around five business areas — Catalog (products and categories), Customers (account records and active status), Orders (order creation and line items), Inventory (stock levels and reservations), and Payments (charging) — all backed by one persistence layer (ShopDbContext). Given how few files exist in this reference implementation, only the core order-placement spine is confidently evidenced end-to-end; there is no evidence of order lookup/history, category-filtered browsing endpoints, payment-status lookup, or customer status management, so those were not included as separate use cases.

useCases.title: Place an order
useCases.description: A customer submits a request to buy one or more products; the system prices, validates, and reserves stock for the order before recording it.
steps: Customer submits a place-order request listing the desired products and quantities
System looks up current pricing for each requested product from the catalog
System verifies the customer's account is active before proceeding
System reserves the requested stock for each product in inventory
Order and its line items are created and the order total is calculated
Order is stored with an initial status
useCases.evidence: OrdersController.Place, OrderService.PlaceOrder, PlaceOrderRequest, LineDto; CustomerService.IsActive, Customer.Active; InventoryService.Reserve, StockItem.Quantity/ProductId; CatalogService.PriceOf

useCases.title: Browse the product catalog
useCases.description: A shopper views the list of products available for purchase, organized into categories.
steps: Shopper requests the list of products
System returns the available products from the catalog, including each product's category

useCases.title: View a product's details and price
useCases.description: A shopper looks up a specific product to see its details and current price before buying.
steps: Shopper requests a product by its ID
System looks up the product and its price
Product details and price are returned

useCases.title: Look up a customer account
useCases.description: A customer's account record is retrieved, e.g. to view or verify account details.
steps: A request is made for a customer by ID
System retrieves the matching customer record

useCases.title: Pay for an order
useCases.description: A customer pays for a placed order, charging a payment that is linked back to that order and recorded with an amount and status.
steps: Customer initiates payment for a specific order
A payment record is created, linked to the order via its order ID, with amount and status recorded
